title: John Backus and the Invention of FORTRAN at IBM (1954-1957)
source_title: ACM A.M. Turing Award: John Backus Citation & Biography
content: In 1954, computer scientist John W. Backus submitted a proposal to his managers at IBM entitled 'Preliminary Report, Specifications for The IBM Mathematical FORmula TRANslating System, FORTRAN.' At the time, programming computers like the IBM 704 required painstaking hand-coded assembly, and software costs routinely exceeded hardware expenses. Skeptics widely believed that high-level compilers could never generate machine code comparable in execution efficiency to hand-tuned human assembly. Backus and his 10-person team spent three years inventing the world's first true optimizing compiler. Released in April 1957, FORTRAN cut the number of programming statements required by a factor of twenty while producing machine code that ran almost as fast as human-written assembly, permanently launching the software engineering discipline.
